Hewisedawi Band (Pit River Tribe)

Also find this entry through: Hewisedawi Band

Hewisedawi is one of the Pit River Tribe’s eleven autonomous bands. The Tribe publishes a band-specific history centered on Goose Lake and neighboring country, describing dispossession, survival and continuing community relationships. This initial reading route preserves that local scope and remains unfinished.

Names & relationshipsThe Pit River Tribe names Hewisedawi as one of eleven autonomous constituent bands. This individual band route is distinct from broader language/people labels and from the collective tribal government. No claim that each band is a separately federally recognized government or that the collective four-county statement defines this band’s boundaries.

These are selected starting points. The full annotated collection, source perspectives, inspection limits and remaining research questions follow below. A starting guide is not an exhaustive history or community endorsement.

01

A community account centered on Goose Lake

The Tribe’s Hewisedawi account centers a community around Goose Lake and neighboring plateau country. It describes seasonal movement among foods and later disruption by settler livestock and fencing. These are the page’s local historical claims, not a uniform chronology for every Pit River band.

Read the sources [1] Pit River Tribe

02

Survival and continuing relationships

The same account describes people surviving displacement through less accessible places and camps near settler towns. It explicitly presents Hewisedawi as a continuing community, with people living in Modoc County and farther afield. Its account of enduring relationships with places should be read with its publication context, without inferring present population, access permission or land title.

Read the sources [1] Pit River Tribe
